items.followUp: What is facilitated diffusion? Give one example.

rubric.why: Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient and requires energy.
rubric.description: Defines active transport as movement against the concentration gradient using energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both movement against the gradient and energy use.

rubric.why: Mineral-ion uptake by root hairs is an example of active transport.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of active transport.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example, such as root hairs absorbing mineral ions.

modelAnswer: Active transport is the movement of substances across a cell membrane against their concentration gradient, using energy (ATP).
For example, root hairs absorb mineral ions from the soil by active transport.

items.followUp: Describe how a planarian can regenerate.

rubric.why: Regeneration involves replacing or regrowing lost or damaged body parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that lost or damaged body parts are replaced or regrown.

rubric.why: Cell division and differentiation produce the cells and tissues needed for regeneration.
rubric.description: Describes the cellular process involved in regeneration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cells divide and differentiate to form the required tissues.

modelAnswer: Regeneration is the process by which lost body parts are replaced or damaged body parts regrow.
Cells at the affected region divide and differentiate to form the missing tissues.
